questions.question: Which of the following is a paddy crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rice.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paddy crop is another name for rice, hence option 1 is correct.**
 
• Rice is a staple food crop that is grown in many countries across the world.
 
• **Cotton** is a** fiber crop** that is grown for its soft, fluffy fibers which are used to make textiles.
 
• ** Cucumber** is a** vegetable crop **that is grown for its crisp and refreshing taste.
 
• **Jute **is a fiber crop that is used to** make burlap and other types of coarse fabric**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kharif

 
 
• Kharif crops are grown with the onset of monsoon in different parts of the country and these are harvested in September-October.
 
• Important crops grown during this season are paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, tur (arhar), moong, urad, cotton, jute, groundnut, and soyabean.
 
• Some of the most important rice-growing regions are Assam, West Bengal, coastal regions of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Maharashtra, particularly the (Konkan coast) along with Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
• Recently, paddy has also become an important crop of Punjab and Haryana.
 
• In states like Assam, West Bengal, and Odisha, three crops of paddy are grown in a year. These are Aus, Aman, and Boro.
 
 
 
• Rabi
 
 
• Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December and harvested in summer from April to June.
 
• Some of the important rabi crops are wheat, barley, peas, gram, and mustard.
 
• Though these crops are grown in large parts of India, states from the north and north-western parts such as Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu, and Kashmir, Uttarakhand, and Uttar Pradesh are important for the production of wheat and other rabi crops.
 
• Availability of precipitation during winter months due to the western temperate cyclones helps in the success of these crops. However, the success of the green revolution in Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh, and parts of Rajasthan has also been an important factor in the growth of the above-mentioned rabi crops. 
 
 
 
• Zaid
 
 
• In between the rabi and the Kharif seasons, there is a short season during the summer months known as the Zaid season.
 
• Some of the crops produced during ‘zaid’ are watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables, and fodder crops.
 
• Sugarcane takes almost a year to grow.

questions.question: A budget document that relates to the assets and liabilities in the capital account of the government, is referred as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**capital budget.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A capital budget is a budget document that specifically focuses on the assets and liabilities in the capital account of the government. This includes investments in infrastructure, buildings, equipment, and other long-term assets.**
 
• The capital budget is different from the revenue budget, which focuses on the day-to-day operating expenses of the government.
 
• The zero budget is a budgeting approach that requires every expense to be justified every year, regardless of whether it was included in the previous year's budget.
 
• A long-term budget is a budget document that covers a period of several years, usually 3-5 years, and includes both capital and operating expenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• ** The capital budget **is an important tool for governments to plan and prioritize their investments in long-term assets. It helps ensure that there is adequate funding for critical infrastructure projects.
 
• **The revenue budget** is also important, as it covers the day-to-day expenses of the government, such as salaries, utilities, and supplies.
 
• **The zero-budget **approach is often used by businesses and organizations to ensure that every expense is justified and necessary.
 
• ** Long-term budgeting** is important for governments, as it allows them to plan for the future and ensure that there is adequate funding for important projects.

questions.question: As of November 2022, who is the President of Bharatiya Janata Party, a political party in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jagat Prakash Nadda.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The current President of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) as of November 2022 is Jagat Prakash Nadda.**
 
• Amit Shah served as the President of BJP from 2014 to 2020 and is currently serving as the Union Home Minister of India.
 
• Narendra Modi is the current Prime Minister of India and a member of BJP, but he is not the President of the party.
 
• Swatantra Dev Singh is the President of Uttar Pradesh BJP, but he is not the national President of the party.
 
• BJP is one of the major political parties in India and has been in power at the national level since 2014.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Bharatiya Janta Party was founded in 1980 as a result of a split in the Janata Party over the issue of dual membership. **
 
• The Bharatiya Jana Sangh constituent of the Janata Party formed the Bharatiya Janata Party after leaving the Janata Party (BJP).
 
• The BJP is often referred to as the Bharatiya Jana Sangh's rebirth.
 
• In 1951, Syama Prasad Mukherjee established BJP.
 
• **Atal Bihari Vajpayee became the party's first president when it was founded in 1980.**
 
• The BJP won only two seats in the first Lok Sabha election after its formation in 1984, but the BJP began to have electoral success in 1989. 
 
• The BJP ran as the organiser of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), a coalition of more than 20 national and regional parties in the 1999 legislative elections.

questions.question: The inscriptions of the Pallavas mention a number of local assemblies. These included the _____, which was an assembly of brahmin land owners.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** sabha.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 2, "sabha," which was an assembly of Brahmin landowners mentioned in the inscriptions of the Pallavas.**
 
• ** "Naukayan"** refers to a leader of a group of boats or ships, "parishad" refers to a council or committee, and "**bhraman"** is not a term commonly used in this context.
 
• The concept of local assemblies was important in the political organization of ancient India, and the Pallavas were one of the dynasties that ruled over parts of southern India during the early medieval period (3rd to 9th centuries CE).
 
• The role and composition of these assemblies varied across different regions and time periods, but they were generally involved in decision-making and dispute resolution related to local governance, land use, and social issues.
 
• The mention of Brahmin landowners in this context suggests that the Pallava sabha may have had a specific role in managing land rights and property disputes among this privileged social group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The inscriptions of the Pallavas mention a number of local assemblies.
 
• These assemblies functioned through subcommittees, which looked after irrigation, agricultural operations, making roads, local temples, etc.
 
• The Nagaram was an organization of merchants.
 
• It is likely that these assemblies were controlled by rich and powerful landowners and merchants.
 
• There were three types of places during this time:
 
 
• Ur - This is the place where the peasants lived and were headed by a headman who collected and paid the taxes.
 
• Sabha - Land granted to Brahmins and was also called Agrahara villages. 
 
• Nagaram - Where merchants and traders resided

questions.question: Which mountain range prevents the cold Siberian winds from entering India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the Himalayas.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Himalayas are the mountain range that prevents the cold Siberian winds from entering India.**
 
• These winds are extremely **cold and dry and can cause a lot of damage to crops and other vegetation if they were to enter India.**
 
• The Himalayas are the highest mountain range in the world, and they run across the northern border of India.
 
• They are also home to some of the highest peaks in the world, including Mount Everest.
 
• The Satpura Range is a mountain range in central India, and it does not prevent the cold Siberian winds from entering India. The Aravali Hills are a range of mountains in western India, and they also do not prevent the cold Siberian winds from entering India.
 
• The Western Ghats are a mountain range that runs along the western coast of India, and they do not prevent the cold Siberian winds from entering India. However, they do play an important role in the monsoon season by blocking the southwest monsoon winds from entering the interior of India.

questions.question: Which among the following classical dance forms was originally known as Sadir Attam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Bharatnatyam__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bharatnatyam

 
 
• Bharatanatyam of Tamil Nadu in Southern India has grown out of the art of dancers dedicated to temples and was earlier known as Sadir or Dasi Attam.
 
• It is the first of India's traditional dances to be refashioned by theatre artists and to be exhibited widely both at home and abroad.
 
• Bharatanatyam rests on principles of performance and aesthetics set down in classics such as Bharata's Natyashastra.
 
• It has a rich repertoire of songs in Telugu, Tamil, and Sanskrit.
 
• The music of Bharatanatyam belongs to the Carnatic system of southern India.
 
• The musicians accompanying a dance recital include at least one vocalist, a Mridangam (drum)-player, a flutist or violinist, or Veena (lute)-player.
 
• The group also includes a Nattuvanar, or dance conductor, who recites the dance syllables as he plays a pair of small bronze cymbals.

questions.question: Economists have found that a poor nation can only progress only if they have good ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the Industrial Sector.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The industrial sector is the correct answer as it provides employment opportunities to a large number of people and contributes significantly to the economic growth of a country.
 
• The industrial sector helps in the development of infrastructure, technology, and innovation, which further boosts the growth of other sectors.
 
• The agricultural sector is important for a country's food security and provides employment opportunities to a large number of people. However, it may not contribute significantly to the economic growth of a country.
 
• The service sector includes industries like healthcare, education, tourism, and hospitality, which are important for the overall development of a country. However, it may not be the main factor for the economic progress of a poor nation.
 
• The private sector includes businesses owned and operated by individuals or groups. It plays a crucial role in the economic development of a country by creating jobs and generating wealth. However, it may not be the only factor in the progress of a poor nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sectors in Economy:

 
 
• Primary Sector:

 
 
• To keep the day-to-day operations going, this sector's services are completely reliant on the availability of natural resources.
 
• Eg. Agriculture, Mining, Fishing, Forestry, Dairy, etc. 
 
 
 
• Secondary Sector:
 
 
• The economics of the sector is based on natural materials that are utilized to manufacture the services and goods that are given, and which are then consumed.
 
 
 
• Tertiary Sector:
 
 
• The tertiary sector is referred to as the service sector.
 
• The service business creates services rather than finished items.
 
• Services (also known as "Intangible Products") include things like attention, direction, access, experience, and emotional labor.

• **SAMADHAN portal is an online platform for registration of industrial disputes that aims to simplify and expedite the process of obtaining justice for workmen.**

• The conciliation officer is responsible for facilitating negotiations between the parties involved in the dispute and attempting to reach an amicable settlement.

• **Micronutrients are essential nutrients required in small quantities by the human body for optimal health and functioning.**
 
• Iron is a micronutrient that plays a crucial role in the production of** red blood cells and the transport of oxygen throughout the body.**
 
• Carbohydrates are macronutrients that provide energy to the body, but they are not considered micronutrients.
 
• Fibre is a type of carbohydrate that **cannot be digested by the body and helps to regulate digestion and prevent constipation, but it is also not considered a micronutrient.**
 
• Water is also not considered a micronutrient, but it is** essential for hydration and many bodily functions.**
 
• Carbohydrates are one of the three macronutrients, along with** proteins and fats.**
 
• Fibre is found in plant-based foods such as fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and legumes.
 
• Water makes up approximately 60% of the human body and is necessary for many bodily processes, including regulating body temperature, transporting nutrients, and removing waste.

questions.question: What was the female literacy rate of India as per the Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 65.46%.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The female literacy rate in India has been steadily increasing over the years, with the 2011 Census showing a significant improvement from the previous Census in 2001, which reported a female literacy rate of 54.16%.**
 
• The literacy rate is the** percentage of people who can read and write in a given population.**
 
• The literacy rate in India has been steadily increasing over the years, with the overall literacy rate in the country being 74.04% as per the Census 2011.
 
• The male literacy rate in India as per the Census 2011 was 82.14%, which is higher than the female literacy rate of 65.46%.
 
• -The difference between male and female literacy rates in India is still significant, with efforts being made to bridge the gap through various government initiatives and programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Literacy level and educational attainment are vital developmental indicators in a developing nation like India as they are key variables of measure of development as they indicate the quality of life, awareness level, and also the level of skill of people in the society.
 
• Better literacy and educational level definitely have a positive impact on health parameters.
 
• Education parameters have an equal weightage in the Human Development Index as well.
 
• Considering the importance of education, India has enacted the Right to Education to ensure free and compulsory education for children in the age group 6- 14 years. 
 
• As per the Census of 2011, the male and female literacy rates were 82.14% and 65.46%.
 
• According to the 2011 census, the literacy rate in India is 74.04%. 
 
• Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India and the 7th Census after independence. 8 Census have been conducted prior to independence.
 
• Census in conducted every 10 years in India. The first Census in India was conducted in the year 1872.
 
• Census includes the total process of collecting, compiling, analyzing, evaluating, publishing and disseminating statistical data regarding the population and housing and their geographical location.

questions.question: What are the products formed when lead reacts with copper chloride?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lead chloride and copper.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **When lead reacts with copper chloride, lead chloride and copper are formed**.
 
• This is because lead has a higher reactivity than copper, so it displaces copper from the compound.
 
• When a lead metal reacts with a solution of copper chloride, then Lead chloride is ____formed__.
 __
 
• When a strip of lead metal is placed in a solution of copper chloride then lead chloride and copper are formed.
 
• Green colour copper chloride feds to colors less solution. because lead is more reactive than copper it displays copper from copper chloride solution.
 
• Pb +CuCl₂ = PbL₂ +Cu
 
 
 
• Lead chloride is a white crystalline solid that is soluble in water. It is often used in the production of other lead compounds and as a reagent in chemical reactions.
 
• Copper is a reddish-brown metal that is a good conductor of electricity. It is commonly used in electrical wiring, plumbing, and as a component in alloys such as brass and bronze.
 
• copper oxide and lead chloride, is incorrect because copper oxide is not formed when lead reacts with copper chloride.
 
• lead oxide and copper hydroxide, is also incorrect because copper hydroxide is not formed in this reaction.
 
• Lead oxide and copper, is incorrect because copper is not oxidized in this reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• A combination reaction is a reaction where two or more elements or compounds combine to form a single compound. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: X + Y → XY.
 
• The combination of two or more elements to form one compound is called a combination reaction.
 
• Other types of Chemical Reactions:
 
 
• Decomposition reaction__: The opposite of a combination reaction, a complex molecule breaks down to make simpler ones. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: AB → A + B.
 
• __Precipitation reaction__: Two solutions of soluble salts are mixed resulting in an insoluble solid (precipitate) forming. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + Soluble salt B → Precipitate + soluble salt C.
 
• __Neutralization reaction__: An acid and a base react with each other. Generally, the product of this reaction is salt and water. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: Acid + Base → Salt + Water.
 
• __Combustion reaction__: Oxygen combines with a compound to form carbon dioxide and water. These reactions are exothermic, meaning they give off heat. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + O2 → H2O + CO2.
 
• __Displacement reaction__: One element takes place with another element in the compound. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + BC → AC + B.

questions.question: With which country did India had a war in the region of the McMahon line in 1962?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** China.**__
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the Prime Minister of India during the Indo-China war in 1962.
 
• India was attacked on October 20, 1962, in what famously came to be known as the Sino-India war of 1962 in the region of the McMahon line.
 
• The war continued for about a month and ended on November 21, after China declared a ceasefire.
 
• When China announced that it would be occupying Tibet, India sent a letter of protest proposing negotiations on the Tibet issue.
 
• China was more active in deploying troops on the Aksai-Chin border.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• India was so concerned about its relations with China that it did not even attend a conference for the conclusion of a peace treaty with Japan because China was not invited.

 
• 
 
• In 1954, China and India concluded the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence i.e. Panchsheel principles.

 
 
• Under this agreement, India acknowledged Chinese rule in Tibet.
 
 
 
• Chinese maps showed some 120,000 square kilometers of Indian territory as Chinese.
 
• China felt humiliated by the reception Dalai Lama obtained in India when he fled there in March 1959.
 
• Tensions increased between the two nations when Mao stated that the Lhasa rebellion in Tibet was caused by Indians.
 
• China's perception of India as a threat to its rule of Tibet became one of the most prominent reasons for the Sino-Indian War.
 
• On October 20, 1962, China's People's Liberation Army invaded India in Ladakh, and across the McMahon Line in the then North-East Frontier Agency.
 
• The Chinese also cut Indian telephone lines, preventing the defenders from making contact with their headquarters.
 
• India, thinking that the war would not take place, did not prepare itself for the war.
 
• The war ended on November 21, after China declared a ceasefire.
